description: Where grpc-gateway and the route fixtures part, found by routes.mjs on 2026-10-15 against grpc-gateway v2.32.0 with its defaults (runtime.NewServeMux()), proxying over gRPC to connect-go v2.0.1 (conformance/README.md, design section 7). The fields are known-divergent-vanguard.json's: servedApart, bindings protoc-gen-grpc-gateway will not generate beside the others, served by a second gateway mux under /gateway/layer/1; fixtures, those whose live call does not agree with the fixture, `observed` matched against the runner's result; probes, requests the runtime does not make, where the two transcoders answer differently. Paths are under /gateway.

servedApart.reason: PATCH /v1/messages/{message_id} is UpdateMessage's route too; protoc-gen-grpc-gateway refuses to generate the second ("duplicate annotation: method=PATCH, template=/v1/messages/{message_id}"), so buf.gen.gateway.yaml leaves the method out and buf.gen.gateway-apart.yaml generates it alone. GetMessage's first and third bindings, both GET /v1/messages/*, are generated, since their templates differ; see the fixture below.

fixtures.fixture: a variable with a multi-segment template
fixtures.answer: 200, echoing {"messageId":"123456"}: GetMessage binding 2's reading of the path, not binding 0's {"name":"messages/123456"}
fixtures.reading: Neither is wrong; the rule cannot be served whole. GetMessage's binding 0, GET /v1/{name=messages/*}, and binding 2, GET /v1/messages/{message_id}, match the same paths. Vanguard refuses the second (known-divergent-vanguard.json); grpc-gateway generates both, and its mux tries the binding registered last first, so binding 2 takes every path binding 0 matches. The runtime builds binding 0's request as the fixture says.

fixtures.fixture: a single-segment variable escapes / and every reserved character
fixtures.reading: The runtime. http.proto has a single-segment variable percent-encode every character but the unreserved ones, / included, and a server decode them. grpc-gateway's default unescaping mode (UnescapingModeLegacy) splits the decoded path, so %2F becomes a separator and the path has a segment too many. With runtime.WithUnescapingMode(runtime.UnescapingModeAllExceptReserved), which grpc-gateway documents as the next default, it echoes the fixture's name (tried by hand, 2026-10-15); the example keeps the default, as a deployed gateway most likely does.

fixtures.fixture: well-known types in their JSON string forms
fixtures.reading: The runtime. A FieldMask's JSON form is its paths in lowerCamelCase, joined by commas, which a reader converts to field names; grpc-gateway's query parser splits the value on commas and keeps each path as written (runtime/query.go), so the service receives the path displayName, which no field has. The echo comes back over gRPC whole, and the gateway then fails writing it as JSON, answering UNKNOWN. mask=display_name is accepted, but is not the JSON form. Timestamp and Duration agree.

fixtures.fixture: a body field is sent whole, a field the path holds included (AIP-134)
fixtures.reading: The runtime, as above: the gateway keeps the update mask's path displayName as written, so the service receives a mask naming no field. Here the service's echo cannot write that request as JSON and fails, which connect-go reports as UNKNOWN without a message; a service applying the mask would refuse it or ignore it. The path and body agree.

fixtures.fixture: a path value under an unset message is its default; defaults are written
fixtures.answer: 200, echoing inner and inner.deep set and empty
fixtures.reading: Neither is wrong; the wire cannot say it. As under Vanguard (known-divergent-vanguard.json): a path segment sets its field and every message on the way, so no path leaves inner unset.

fixtures.fixture: an unset body field is an empty object
fixtures.reading: Neither is wrong; the wire cannot say it. As under Vanguard: with body: "message" a body of {} is the field set and empty.

probes.name: an unknown query parameter
probes.reading: Neither is wrong; see known-divergent-vanguard.json. grpc-gateway drops a parameter that names no field.

probes.name: a verb the path has no route for
probes.reading: Neither is wrong; see known-divergent-vanguard.json. grpc-gateway answers UNIMPLEMENTED with its HTTP mapping, 501.

probes.name: PATCH without an update mask
probes.reading: Neither is wrong; see known-divergent-vanguard.json. grpc-gateway fills update_mask with the fields the body sets, in no fixed order.
